`IAgent.listPluginInstallations` exposes provider-owned persisted plugin records through the local management bridge. The Copilot implementation uses global SDK `plugins.list`, not session-effective `session.plugins.list` or the client's plugin discovery inventory. Disabled installations remain installed; built-ins and managed desired entries with `installed: false` do not become user installations. Session-only/client-provided plugins are not installation records. Mutations retain the selected backend session/chat routing and complete on the SDK transaction, without waiting for client discovery.

+Local management IPC also supports listing, adding, and browsing plugin marketplaces without a session. Copilot uses the global SDK client when no session is supplied, as it does for session-free plugin installation; it does not create a temporary chat or trust the receiving workspace. Existing session-addressed callers retain their exact chat routing. This is a local management capability, not an extension of the Agent Host Protocol.

The workbench marketplace install provider projects these records into `IRecordedCustomizationMarketplaceResource` and uses their opaque direct-source IDs to disambiguate uninstall. SDK inventories expose optional resolved `rootPath` and opaque `id` metadata; neither is an enable/disable or uninstall argument. Do not infer roots from `installedFrom` (a live marketplace directory) or private cache layouts. Retained catalog selections can be associated with a unique installed name/repository/revision match; ambiguous matches are left unassociated. Catalog association is in-memory, not a reconstructed durable receipt, and plugin targets have no invented filesystem URI.

Uninstall requires exactly one current SDK identity match, and direct installs require a nonempty SDK direct-source ID; repository/revision metadata cannot substitute for the SDK's uninstall discriminator. Harnesses that provide `marketplaceManagementProvider` own their marketplace inventory and mutations. The management UI uses that provider exclusively and does not merge `chat.plugins.marketplaces`; each available provider marketplace is also projected as an independently selectable Discover source backed by the provider's browse operation. Harnesses without the capability retain the VS Code configuration-backed marketplace flow. Runtime-backed providers remain authoritative for managed-policy enforcement.

-External `vscode://chat-plugin/add-marketplace?ref=owner/repo` and `vscode://chat-plugin/install?source=owner/repo&plugin=name` links use the Copilot Agent Host harness exclusively, never the configuration-backed marketplace or legacy plugin installer. Marketplace sources may also be URL-escaped Git URLs or base64-encoded references; plugin names are plain query-parameter values. Both routes require explicit consent before a marketplace mutation or plugin installation. They reuse an existing Copilot Agent Host session, or ask before opening and provisioning a new one. Installation first adds the marketplace, then resolves the exact named plugin through that marketplace's provider and installs it in the same session. Runtime policy enforcement remains authoritative, and failures do not fall back to another harness.

+External `vscode://chat-plugin/add-marketplace?ref=owner/repo` and `vscode://chat-plugin/install?source=owner/repo&plugin=name` links target Copilot-native or VS Code-managed shared installation on the receiving machine, followed by source- and destination-aware consent. An optional `harness=copilot` or `harness=vscode` selects the owner and skips the target picker, but never bypasses consent; links without a harness ask the user to select the owner. Empty, repeated, and unsupported values are rejected. Sources may be URL-escaped Git URLs or base64-encoded references, including `#revision`; plugin names are plain query-parameter values. Copilot uses local management IPC and global SDK marketplace and plugin operations without creating or trusting a chat session or the open workspace. Unpinned Awesome Copilot plugin links resolve through the enabled GitHub Feed and its existing owner installation provider; other plugin links add the exact marketplace source, resolve the named plugin in that marketplace, and install its runtime-owned identity. VS Code uses its source installer and configuration-backed marketplace inventory, preserving marketplace trust and strict policy checks. Shared installation does not imply native Claude/Codex ownership or compatibility. Remote-workspace and web windows reject these links, failures never switch owners, and runtime policy enforcement remains authoritative for Copilot.

Harnesses may supply an `ICustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider`. Its SDK or runtime inventory is authoritative for installation identity, ownership, recovery, and removal; the workbench does not create a second durable installation record. The install service removes legacy machine-profile installation records without reading or migrating them. It projects provider inventory through the same immutable snapshot used by Skills, MCP, Discover, and management actions, and keeps only a bounded, in-memory association between a provider installation and catalog presentation metadata seen in the current window. That association can enrich installed rows with icons and descriptions but cannot make a resource installed. Provider inventory remains usable when the catalog is offline or no longer returns an entry, with fallback type icons and retained SDK catalog metadata.
